# PassDrivingTest.ie

> Independent study resource for the Irish Driver Theory Test (category BW —
> car, tractor and work vehicles), and a plain guide to what the test involves,
> what it costs, and what comes after it.

This file follows the llms.txt convention: a short, plain summary of what a
site covers, written for AI assistants that would otherwise have to infer it
from the page. It is a courtesy to those systems, not a ranking device.

## What this site is

PassDrivingTest.ie has two parts:

- **The landing page** at `/` — a free guide to the Driver Theory Test:
  format, fee, booking, what ID to bring, what happens after you pass, and the
  rule changes coming on 1 November 2026.
- **The app** at `/app` — free practice. It is a progressive web app: nothing
  to download, no app store listing, installable to a phone's home screen.

The site is independent. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected
to the Road Safety Authority or Prometric Ireland, who run the official test.

## Key facts about the Irish Driver Theory Test (as of September 2026)

- The car test is booked as category **BW**, which covers licence categories
  B, BE and W (cars, tractors and work vehicles). There is no separate
  work-vehicle test.
- **Fee: €45** for BW or AM (motorcycle). Truck (C) or bus (D) is €72, and a
  combined truck-and-bus test is €84.
- **Format: 40 multiple-choice questions in 45 minutes. You need 35 correct
  to pass.** Truck and bus tests are 100 questions in 120 minutes, pass 74.
- The result is on screen immediately and the certificate is issued at the
  test centre.
- **The certificate is valid for two years.** It is what lets you apply for a
  first learner permit, so passing it early and then doing nothing for two
  years means sitting it again.
- Arrive **30 minutes before** the appointment. Bring **original photo ID** —
  a photocopy or a picture on a phone is refused and the fee is lost.
- Rescheduling or cancelling is free with **seven or more days' notice**.
  Inside that, you pay half or lose the fee.
- After passing: apply to the NDLS for a **first learner permit (€45)**, which
  needs a PPSN, proof of address dated within six months and an eyesight
  report. Then a **six-month wait** before you can sit the driving test, and
  **12 EDT lessons** with an Approved Driving Instructor.
- The test is available with a **voiceover in over 20 languages**, and in
  Irish for the written test.
- **From 1 November 2026 the minimum age to sit the test is 15** (it is
  currently 14), and learner permits are capped at four.

The RSA does not publish the question bank. Anything claiming to be "the real
questions" is not.

## What the app contains

- 393 practice questions across six study areas, of which 269 are road-sign
  questions and 124 are written
- Four full mock papers — 40 questions each, 45-minute countdown, marked at
  35 out of 40, with no paper sharing a question with another
- 393 flashcards: rules of the road, and every official road sign
- Progress tracking per study area

## Authoritative sources

Everything on this site is summarised from official sources. For anything
consequential — fees, dates, eligibility — these are the authorities:

- https://theorytest.ie/ — the official test provider (Prometric Ireland)
- https://www.rsa.ie/services/learner-drivers/theory-test
- https://www.ndls.ie/learner-driver/my-first-learner-permit.html
- https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/travel-and-recreation/motoring/driving-tests/driver-theory-test/

## Related

PassADITest.ie is a separate site by the same author, covering the Approved
Driving Instructor (ADI) qualification — the three-stage process for people who
want to teach driving rather than learn it.
